name: Auth + RBAC/ownership
description: Adds session authentication plus role-based access control and per-record ownership checks on top of an existing stack pack. Deliberately dependency-free: sessions are signed with node:crypto HMAC and passwords hashed with scrypt, and the framework's own cookie API carries them, so the capability adds no third-party auth library and no supply-chain surface. Verified against reference-apps/nextjs-postgres-crud.

inputs.name: sessionStrategy
inputs.description: How sessions are issued and verified.

inputs.name: roles
inputs.description: Comma-separated list of role names to seed.

setup.description: Generate and document the HMAC secret that signs session cookies. It is the one piece of configuration this capability cannot infer, and rotating it invalidates every session.
Adds the role enum and the ownership column as a real migration rather than an ad-hoc schema edit, so the change is reversible and auditable.

requiredArtifacts.description: Password hashing, session signing and session reading — the only place that touches the session cookie.
Role and per-record ownership checks, called first by every route that touches an owned record.
Network-boundary guard that rejects unauthenticated requests to protected paths before any handler or database call runs.
Contains the migration introducing the role enum and ownership column.

verification.description: Authenticated, unauthenticated and cross-tenant access attempts are all exercised.

operationalEvidence.evidence: Every generated API route is wrapped in the ownership/role guard by default, and the test suite asserts a 403 on cross-tenant access.
